title: The Logic of a Prompt & Life

parts.name: Act as
parts.line: A role for the model to take on, which sets its vocabulary, depth and point of view.
parts.weak: Give me tips for my vegetable garden.
strong: Act as an experienced community gardener.
Give me tips for my vegetable garden.
parts.guess: Which expert voice, level of detail and angle you want.

parts.name: Audience
parts.line: Who will read or use the answer, and what they already know.
parts.weak: Explain how a mortgage works.
strong: Explain how a mortgage works
to someone buying their first home who has never taken out a loan.
parts.guess: Whether to explain the basics or skip them, and which words the reader knows.

parts.name: Tone
parts.line: The emotional colour of the reply: friendly, formal, firm, playful or calm.
parts.weak: Write a message telling my team the picnic is cancelled.
strong: Write a
warm, upbeat
message telling my team the picnic is cancelled.
parts.guess: Whether to sound warm, neutral, formal or blunt.

parts.name: Language
parts.line: Which language to answer in, and how plain or technical the wording should be.
parts.weak: Write instructions for my neighbour on watering my plants.
strong: Write instructions
in simple Spanish
for my neighbour on watering my plants.
parts.guess: Which language, spelling and reading level to use.

parts.name: Context
parts.line: The background facts of your situation that the answer should build on.
parts.weak: Suggest a dinner I can cook tonight.
strong: I have rice, eggs, spinach and twenty minutes, and my partner is vegetarian.
Suggest a dinner I can cook tonight.
parts.guess: Your situation, so it fills the gap with a typical case that may not be yours.

parts.name: Examples
parts.line: One or more samples of what a good answer looks like.
parts.weak: Suggest names for my new grey kitten.
strong: Suggest names for my new grey kitten.
Names I like: Pebble, Smudge, Biscuit.
parts.guess: The style, length and pattern you have in your head.

parts.name: Keywords
parts.line: Words or names that must appear, or that pin down the topic.
parts.weak: Write a short bio for my bakery's website.
strong: Write a short bio for my bakery's website.
Mention sourdough, our family recipes and the Saturday market.
parts.guess: Which specific names, things or ideas you care about.

parts.name: Terminology
parts.line: Definitions for the words in your request that could mean more than one thing.
parts.weak: Give me a training plan for a long-distance race.
strong: Give me a training plan for a long-distance race.
By long-distance I mean a 10 km race, not a marathon.
parts.guess: Which meaning of an ambiguous word you have in mind.

parts.name: Scope
parts.line: What the answer should cover, and what it should leave out.
parts.weak: Tell me about the history of bicycles.
strong: Tell me about the history of bicycles
from 1860 to 1900, covering design changes only, not racing.
parts.guess: How wide or narrow to go, and what counts as off topic.

parts.name: Limitations
parts.line: Rules the answer must obey, such as length, cost or things to avoid.
parts.weak: Suggest a birthday party activity for ten-year-olds.
strong: Suggest a birthday party activity for ten-year-olds
that works indoors, needs no screens and uses only things most homes already have.
parts.guess: Your hard limits, so it may suggest things you cannot use.

parts.name: Deadline
parts.line: The time frame your task, or the information you need, belongs to.
parts.weak: Make a study plan for my driving test.
strong: Make a study plan for my driving test,
which is three weeks from today.
parts.guess: Which dates matter, and how current the facts must be.

parts.name: Format
parts.line: The shape of the answer: a list, a table, steps, an email or a short paragraph.
parts.weak: Compare walking, cycling and taking the bus to work.
strong: Compare walking, cycling and taking the bus to work
in a table with one row per option.
parts.guess: Whether you want a list, a table, a paragraph or steps.

parts.name: Objective
parts.line: What you want the answer to achieve: the point of the whole request.
parts.weak: Tell me about electric cars.
strong: Tell me about electric cars
so I can decide whether my next car should be one.
parts.guess: Why you are asking, so it cannot tell what is useful.

parts.name: Call to action
parts.line: The next step the answer should end on, for you or for the people who read it.
parts.weak: Write a flyer about our street clean-up.
strong: Write a flyer about our street clean-up
that ends by asking readers to sign up at the library desk.
parts.guess: Whether to end with a next step, and what that step is.

parts.name: Citations
parts.line: Sources the answer should point to, so you can check where each claim comes from.
parts.weak: Explain whether reading in dim light harms your eyes.
strong: Using only the health article pasted below,
explain whether reading in dim light harms your eyes,
and say which paragraph supports each point.
parts.guess: Whether you need sources, and which kinds you trust.

parts.name: Statistics
parts.line: Numbers that support a claim, such as counts, averages or rates.
parts.weak: Write a paragraph on why our town needs a new crossing.
strong: Write a paragraph on why our town needs a new crossing,
using the traffic survey figures pasted below.
parts.guess: Whether you want numbers, and how precise they must be.

parts.name: Quotes
parts.line: Exact words from a real person or text, repeated word for word.
parts.weak: Write a short speech for my grandmother's 90th birthday.
strong: Write a short speech for my grandmother's 90th birthday,
quoting her favourite saying, which I have written out exactly below.
parts.guess: Whether you want quotes, from whom, and how exact.

parts.name: Points of view
parts.line: Other people's perspectives the answer should consider, not only yours.
parts.weak: Should our family get a dog?
strong: Should our family get a dog?
Consider it from the view of the kids, the parents who will walk it, and our elderly neighbour.
parts.guess: Whose interests and views count, so it may give only one side.

parts.name: Counterarguments
parts.line: The strongest objections to an idea, so you can test it before relying on it.
parts.weak: Here is my plan to start selling handmade candles online.
strong: Here is my plan to start selling handmade candles online.
Give me the three strongest reasons it could fail.
parts.guess: Whether you want honest pushback or simple agreement.

parts.name: Analogies
parts.line: A comparison with something familiar that helps explain something new.
parts.weak: Explain how a computer's memory works.
strong: Explain how a computer's memory works
using an analogy from cooking in a kitchen.
parts.guess: Which familiar things you know well enough to compare against.

parts.name: Questions
parts.line: An invitation for the model to ask you what it needs before it answers.
parts.weak: Help me write a cover letter for a job.
strong: Help me write a cover letter for a job.
Before you start, ask me up to five questions about the role and my experience.
parts.guess: Everything you forgot to say, silently filled in with typical defaults.
